alex_support: Hey team — incoming escalation from Acme AI. Their embeddings calls started failing yesterday after a deploy. Error: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768". Happens only when they batch 64 texts in one request. Root logs attached below.

jordan_support: Can you paste the exact request payload (no secrets)?

alex_support: Here's sanitized payload from their TS SDK call:

alex_support: ```ts
const embeddings = await client.embeddings.create({
  model: "redwood-embed-v1",
  input: texts, // array of 64 strings
});
```

alex_support: They say same code works for batch size 1 and 8, fails at 32+.

maria_engineering: @alex_support interesting — dimension mismatch usually means model variant mismatch or post-processing expecting different vector size. Which SDK version are they on?

alex_support: They reported @taylor_sdk client v0.9.2 (typescript). Also they reported using the Python SDK via a microservice with v0.11.0 and saw the same issue.

taylor_sdk: pinging here — we had a change in how batched inputs are encoded in 0.9.x TS SDK. Could be double-encoding when payload > some threshold. Do we have the raw HTTP request body and server response?

alex_support: Server response body (sanitized):

alex_support: ```json
{"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768","request_id":"req_01F...","code":"invalid_embedding"}
```

ethan_infra: Also saw elevated 502/504s on the embeddings pool around the same time window. Could be a partial model swap (quantized vs full) if routing failed — but that's speculative.

maria_engineering: Steps to triage:
1) confirm model selected and model variant (is it `redwood-embed-v1` vs `redwood-embed-v1-quant`)
2) capture the per-request headers the SDK sends (content-type, encoding)
3) reproduce locally with similar batch sizes
4) check for intermediate proxy that might chunk or re-encode the body

alex_support: Customer did confirm they pinned `redwood-embed-v1` — no explicit quant flag. They are in Hosted API (US-East).

jordan_support: Can you ask customer to run a minimal curl repro with batch of 64? Example curl:

jordan_support: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-v1","input":["a","b",...]}'’
```

alex_support: They ran it and curl 64 worked fine. So it's SDK-specific.

taylor_sdk: ok that narrows it. Two SDKs reported: TS 0.9.2 and Python 0.11.0 — maybe they share the underlying HTTP client (our internal http-utils) with a buggy chunking behavior when body > 16KB.

maria_engineering: @taylor_sdk can you check commit history for last month around encoder/streaming changes? Also check how we set `Content-Length` vs `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`.

taylor_sdk: Found suspicious commit in TS that switched to `fetch` with streaming encoder. It may set `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson` accidentally for large arrays. If server sees ndjson it might parse each item individually and return embeddings from a different model pipeline that uses 768 dims. That would explain mismatch.

alex_support: Customer provided a raw capture (snipped):

alex_support: ```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Content-Type: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

{"model":"redwood-embed-v1","input":["...64 items..."]}
```

maria_engineering: Another angle: batching across multiple model partitions might route sub-batches to a fallback quantized model if a node is under memory pressure. If fallback model is 768-dim, mixing results could trigger client-side check and throw error. But server should avoid mixing model variants in the same response.

ethan_infra: Checking infra: around 2025-10-12T16:34: some GPUs were cycled in eu-west and we briefly routed traffic to a warm pool with older quantized images — however customer is US-East. We did have a spike that caused cross-region overflow for some tenant requests. I'll check routing logs for that account.

taylor_sdk: For immediate workaround: advise customer to set batch_size to <= 16 or downgrade to SDK v0.9.1 (if regression introduced in 0.9.2). Also add client-side validation to fallback gracefully if embedding dimension mismatch occurs — return partial results or retry with single-item mode.

jordan_support: They need a reproducible failure we can run internally. @alex_support can you ask for a repro repo or specific encoded payload (base64) so we can reproduce with our TS runtime?

alex_support: Done. They uploaded a small repro that consistently fails for batch_size=64 with TS 0.9.2. Repro instructions included.

maria_engineering: I pulled the repro. Quick triage notes:
- When we run with node 18 and TS SDK 0.9.2, request body arrives split into multiple chunks; when body arrives as multiple frames our server-side NDJSON parser accidentally triggers a different codepath if `input` is streamed item-by-item.
- The bug fixed path: ensure the content-type is JSON and that our ingestion waits for end-of-body before attempting decode.

maria_engineering: Proposed fix (server-side): tighten parser so it only uses streaming NDJSON parser when Content-Type explicitly `application/x-ndjson` OR `chunked=true` AND body contains top-level newlines. But we also should patch the SDK to avoid sending chunked transfer unless streaming mode is explicit.

taylor_sdk: Agreed — I'll push a hotfix to TS SDK to force explicit Content-Length for non-streaming `embeddings.create` and disable automatic chunked streaming for arrays < 200KB.

alex_support: Customer asked about billing spikes — they saw many retries earlier which multiplied their usage. Any mitigation?

jordan_support: We can issue a one-time credits adjustment while we investigate. Submit ticket with request_id and timeframe.

ethan_infra: Infra note: I added a temporary routing rule to prevent cross-region overflow for embeddings for that tenant; it should stop accidental fallback to older quantized nodes.

maria_engineering: Tests to validate fix:
- unit tests in SDK to ensure Content-Length set for small arrays
- integration test: send 64-item batch, assert server receives single JSON body, response dims 1536
- load test: 10k concurrent batched requests to ensure no regression in throughput

taylor_sdk: Patch PR created: https://git.redwood/cli/ts-sdk/pull/452
Patch includes:
- disable chunked transfer for embeddings by default
- better retry metadata for 429 with `retry-after`
- expose `timeoutMs` and `maxRetries` in client config; default timeout increased to 30s for embeddings

alex_support: Customer applied a local patch to set `maxRetries=2` and `timeoutMs=45000` and they reported success — batch of 64 now returns 1536-dim embeddings.

jordan_support: Great. Action items:
- @taylor_sdk backport fix to Python SDK and release patches (0.9.3 TS, 0.11.1 Py)
- @ethan_infra confirm no further cross-region fallbacks for that tenant
- @maria_engineering add server-side parser guard and deploy canary
- @alex_support send credits approval ticket to finance

alex_support: I'll follow up with the customer and keep them in the loop. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-4472 — Embeddings dimension mismatch for batched requests. Severity: P2. Assigned: eng-ml, sdk-team.

maria_engineering: Postmortem notes will include root cause: SDK switched to streaming/chunked encoding + server mis-detection of NDJSON. Remediation: server parser harden + SDK chunking opt-out + better telemetry to detect mixed-model responses.

jordan_support: Closing loop with customer now, will keep thread updated if they see any regressions.
